phase_partition_v3.boundary_rule: early = interval ends at or before steady_after_ns; crossing = interval straddles it (at most one, listed separately); steady = interval starts at or after it. Every interval belongs to exactly one class, so the class sums equal the totals exactly.
phase_partition_v3.closure: all three fields report creep/work_over/release_excess residuals of exactly 0 and classes_are_disjoint true, so there is no 15 ns gap

early_window_finding.statement: both C1 fields lose far more than the baseline inside the first 2 s after the anchor, and the baseline's first 2 s contains no group work overrun at all (work_over exactly 0). This 2-of-2 against 1-of-1 pattern is suggestive, not conclusive.

steady_window_finding.statement: the two C1 fields straddle the single baseline in steady phase, in opposite directions and with a probe-state difference between them, so revision 2's 'steady state 8.8% better' does not survive as a C1 effect and is withdrawn

diagnostic_sampling_disclosure.revision1_error: revision 1 compared step/native stage means and used them to argue that every step became slower. Those streams are not a census.
diagnostic_sampling_disclosure.step_trigger_source: Simulator/wksim_core/joint.py records diagnostic_step_cpu_timing only when (wall_end-wall_start > 2_000_000) or (tick % 250 == 0); the record itself carries the limitation 'Thread CPU separates execution from off-CPU time; off-CPU includes I/O wait and descheduling'
diagnostic_sampling_disclosure.native_trigger_source: diagnostic_native_input_timing is recorded under the same or-trigger and carries the limitation 'Retained slow(>2ms native wait)/periodic(tick%250) samples, not a full census.'
diagnostic_sampling_disclosure.consequence: sample means are conditional on a slow-enriched sample and cannot represent all steps; they are reported only as descriptions of the retained samples and are not used as evidence that every step slowed
diagnostic_sampling_disclosure.sound_metric_used_instead: a step whose measured span exceeds 2 ms is always retained, so the count of retained records with span > 2 ms is an exact count of >2 ms steps
diagnostic_sampling_disclosure.retraction: revision 1 asserted that the added cost was visible in stages that do not perform collection and therefore was not GC. That is retracted: collection time lands inside whichever stage is running, and the baseline's own gen2 pause was bracketed inside _native_wait('px4', ...), i.e. inside native_inputs wall. Stage boundaries do not separate GC from non-GC.

gc_in_shared_window_fact.care: this is a comparison of measured collection pauses only; it does not localize the added latency, because collection time is embedded in the stage timings and the decisive baseline gen2 lies outside this field's lifetime

attribution.statement: Two flag-on fields against one historical flag-off field cannot attribute the early-phase loss to gc.freeze, to the OS, or to the flight controller, and they cannot claim a performance change: the terminal outcome is identical in all three. What they do show is where the lateness is acquired (the first 2 s after the anchor, in both flag-on fields) and that no steady-phase effect reproduces across them.

normalisation_limits: Full-run totals are not comparable: wall 245.117 s vs 269.504 s, terminal tick 96624 vs 109776, groups 24146 vs 27434.
All rate/GC comparisons use the matched window on group start ticks [40, 96620] where both fields contribute exactly 24146 groups / 24145 intervals.
The baseline's only gen2 pause (24326966 ns at tick 107572) lies outside the candidate's lifetime, so the candidate's 'no in-flight gen2' cannot be credited to gc.freeze by this pair.

A metric of the form 'gen2 max pause in [anchor, stop] < 24.33 ms' is satisfied by the candidate without covering the tick where the baseline event occurs; on the matched window both arms have zero gen2.

The 2 s steady_after boundary is NOT excluded by the matched window; the measured 247 of 24146 matched groups (1.02%) fall at or before it. Revision 2's 500 groups / 2.07% came from converting 2 s into 2000 ticks. The phase_partition field now reports the split explicitly instead of leaving the reader to reconstruct it.

n = 1 per arm, no repetition and no interleaving. The main session performs process/load pre-checks and reserves native resources for the field, but a single historical pair cannot control all host load.
diagnostic_step_cpu_timing and diagnostic_native_input_timing are slow-enriched or-triggered samples, not a census; only their trigger counts are treated as exact here.

The rate_timing_probe is diagnostic-only and adds its own overhead (extra monotonic reads, health/sleep wrapper dispatch, sample aggregation, record writing); it is present in both arms but is not subtracted, so release_excess is an instrumented quantity.
No unfreeze cost is measured: gc.unfreeze() is not a collection and emits no diagnostic_gc_timing event.

measurement_gap.kind: localisation and control gap, not a threshold gap
precise: The added loss is localised to the first 2 s after the anchor in both flag-on fields; the analyzer now reports that split, so this is no longer a reporting gap, only an attribution gap.

The probe-free C1 field vwen35gc carries no diagnostic_* stream at all (zero gc_timing, zero step/native CPU timing, zero rate_timing_probe), so it lacks diagnostic stage records for CPU/GC attribution. Ordinary wire events can still be correlated in time; such correlation alone cannot identify the cause of the early loss.

For the probe-on C1 field ztdsk269 the early window (ticks 40..1040) contains exactly one gen0 pause of 29612 ns against 23900631 ns of early creep, so measured GC pause does not explain that window either; the split inside it is work_over 12665444 ns vs release_excess 11235187 ns.
Whether the early loss comes from the freeze's effect, from the 16.492919 ms prepare collect (outside the timed segment), or from conditions in that interval is not separable from these fields.
No steady-phase effect reproduces: the two flag-on fields straddle the baseline in opposite directions (-13.3% and +12.9%).
No matched-window evidence exists at or beyond tick 107572 for any flag-on field, where the baseline's decisive gen2 occurred.
measurement_gap.threshold_note: Nothing here justifies relaxing LATE_LIMIT_NS, the 0.5 requested rate, the 8 ms group period, the 4-tick barrier, or any health bound.
